transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess the main thing is I haven’t really been eating much. It’s probably not a huge deal, but it’s been enough that I thought maybe I should ask somebody.

Like, at work, on my lunch break, I’ll get food I normally like, and then I just kind of stare at it and end up throwing most of it away. I don’t know if that’s… the kind of thing you mean, but that’s what made me come in.
How long have you been experiencing this decrease in appetite?

Um… I think about two months, maybe. It kind of started after I got this window display award at work and the district manager was giving me a lot of attention for it. I know that sounds like a good thing, so I’m not trying to make it into something bigger than it is, but… yeah, around then is when I noticed I wasn’t eating as much.
Have you lost any weight over the past two months?

I… I haven’t really been tracking the number, honestly. My clothes maybe feel a little looser, but I don’t know for sure.

It’s more that I barely want to eat anymore. Like on my lunch break at the store, I’ll get something I used to really like and just sit there staring at it, and then I end up throwing most of it away. I’m sorry, I know that’s not exactly a number.
Are you worried about gaining weight?

No… not really. I’m not trying to lose weight or avoid gaining weight or anything like that.

It’s more just… I barely want to eat. Like at work on my lunch break, I’ll have food I used to like right in front of me, and I just sit there staring at it, and then I end up throwing most of it away. I don’t know if that answers it right.
Are you afraid of eating or afraid of the act of eating in front of others?

No, I don’t think I’m scared of eating, or of people seeing me eat. It’s not like that.

It’s more… I just don’t want the food. Like I’ll be at lunch at the store with something I used to like, and I just stare at it and end up throwing most of it away. That’s actually kind of what made me think I should ask for help, if that makes sense.
Are you enjoying things you used to like, outside of eating?

Yeah… I mean, kind of. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but stuff I used to really look forward to just doesn’t hit the same.

Like gallery nights, playing basketball, getting food-truck tacos, or helping kids with art projects… I used to get excited about that stuff. Lately I’ll show up and just kind of stand there feeling flat, and then I usually make some excuse to leave early. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever find yourself feeling interested or excited about things again, even if it's just for a little while?

A little, maybe… but not like before.

I’ll go to something like a gallery night, or try to play basketball, or even do art stuff with the kids, and I keep waiting for that excited feeling to kick in. Sometimes there’s like a tiny moment where I think, “Okay, this is nice,” but mostly I just feel kind of flat. Then I end up making some excuse to leave early.

I’m not trying to be dramatic or anything… I just don’t really feel interested the way I used to.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

I don’t know if I’d say sad most of the time, exactly. Maybe more like… low, or kind of weighed down.

I can still get through work and talk to people, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart. But yeah, there are a lot of days where I feel pretty down. Is that what you mean by sad?
Are there any activities that you still enjoy and look forward to?

Honestly… not really like I used to. I mean, I still try to do things, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely stopped.

Gallery nights, basketball, grabbing tacos from the food trucks, helping kids with art stuff… those used to be things I’d actually look forward to. Lately I go, and I’m just kind of there. I feel flat, and then I usually end up making some excuse to leave early.

Maybe there are small moments that are okay, but I wouldn’t say I really look forward to much right now. Is that… does that answer it?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you used to find pleasurable?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but those things used to actually get me excited — gallery nights, playing basketball, grabbing tacos from the food trucks, helping kids with art stuff.

Lately I still show up sometimes, but I’m mostly just standing there feeling kind of flat. Then I usually end up making some excuse to leave. So… yeah, I guess I have lost interest, at least compared to how I used to be.
Have you been feeling hopeless about the future?

I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless, exactly. I mean… I don’t feel super optimistic, but I still kind of assume things could get better if I keep showing up and doing what I’m supposed to do.

Some days the future just feels blank, maybe. But “hopeless” sounds a little strong. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about anything?

A little, yeah… I mean, I know people keep telling me I earned it, but I keep thinking I don’t really deserve that award, or even the chance at becoming supervisor.

It feels like maybe I fooled everyone somehow, like they’re seeing something that isn’t really there. And then I feel guilty about it, like I tricked them, even though… logically, I guess I didn’t. Does that make sense?
Have you been experiencing these low feelings nearly every day?

I… I’m not totally sure it’s nearly every day. I mean, it happens a lot, but I don’t want to exaggerate it.

Some days I can kind of get through okay, and other days it’s just there in the background. I guess I haven’t really been tracking it closely. Is that… is that okay to say?
How many days a week would you say you've been feeling this way?

Maybe… most days? I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been kind of hanging around for about two months now.

It started around when I got that window display award and the district manager started paying attention to me. Since then it’s been, I don’t know… probably more days than not. Is that the kind of answer you’re looking for?
For how long have you been feeling low or weighed down?

I think… about two months, maybe. It kind of started after that window display award, when the district manager started noticing me more.

It hasn’t been, like, every single second or anything, but yeah… it’s been around since then. Is that specific enough?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Um… not as much as I used to, I guess.

I used to get pretty excited about stuff like gallery nights, or playing basketball, or even just grabbing tacos from the food trucks. And I liked helping kids with art things when I got the chance.

Lately, though, I kind of just… stand there. I don’t really feel much, and I usually end up making some excuse to leave. I don’t know if that counts as not enjoying things, but it feels different than before.
Have you been feeling low or weighed down for more than half of the days over the past two months?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been more than half the days, probably, for about two months now.

It really started around that window display award and when the district manager started paying more attention to me. Since then it’s just been… kind of there a lot of the time. Does that answer it right?
Would you say that these low feelings have been interfering with your daily life in a significant way?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still making it to work, so it’s not like I’ve completely fallen apart or anything.

But I guess it has been affecting things. I’ve been messing up inventory counts and display plans more than I should, and my manager’s had to double-check my work, which is embarrassing.

And outside work, I’ve been skipping stuff I used to always show up for… gallery nights, basketball, the youth art workshops. I usually just say I’m tired or busy. So… yeah, I guess it’s significant. Is that what you mean?
Have you been experiencing these low feelings for at least two weeks?

Yeah… definitely more than two weeks. I guess it’s been about two months now, since that window display award and when the district manager started paying more attention to me.

I don’t know if I’m explaining it right, but it’s been going on for a while.
